controls.title: Governance and Organisation
controls.description: Financial entities shall have in place an internal governance and control framework that ensures an effective and prudent management of ICT risk.

controls.title: ICT Risk Management Framework
controls.description: Financial entities shall have a sound, comprehensive and well-documented ICT risk management framework as part of their overall risk management system.

controls.title: ICT Systems, Protocols and Tools
controls.description: Financial entities shall identify, classify and adequately document all ICT supported business functions, roles, and ICT assets supporting those functions.

controls.title: Identification
controls.description: Financial entities shall identify all sources of ICT risk, assess cyber threats and ICT vulnerabilities, and review ICT risk scenarios.

controls.title: Protection and Prevention
controls.description: Financial entities shall continuously monitor and control the security and functioning of ICT systems and tools, and minimise the impact of ICT risk through appropriate tools, policies and procedures.

controls.title: Detection
controls.description: Financial entities shall have in place mechanisms to promptly detect anomalous activities, including ICT network performance issues and ICT-related incidents.

controls.title: Response and Recovery
controls.description: Financial entities shall put in place a comprehensive ICT business continuity policy and establish ICT response and recovery plans.

controls.title: Backup Policies and Procedures, Restoration and Recovery
controls.description: Financial entities shall develop and document a backup policy specifying the scope and frequency of backups, and establish restoration and recovery procedures and methods.

controls.title: Learning and Evolving
controls.description: Financial entities shall gather information on vulnerabilities and cyber threats, ICT-related incidents, and analyse the impact and lessons learned from them.

controls.title: Communication
controls.description: Financial entities shall have in place communication plans enabling a responsible disclosure of ICT-related incidents or major vulnerabilities to clients and counterparts.

controls.title: ICT-Related Incident Management Process
controls.description: Financial entities shall define, establish and implement an ICT-related incident management process to detect, manage and notify ICT-related incidents.

controls.title: Classification of ICT-Related Incidents
controls.description: Financial entities shall classify ICT-related incidents and determine their impact based on criteria including number of clients affected, duration, geographical spread, data losses, criticality of services affected, and economic impact.

controls.title: Reporting of Major ICT-Related Incidents
controls.description: Financial entities shall report major ICT-related incidents to the relevant competent authority using initial, intermediate and final notifications.

controls.title: Harmonisation of Reporting Content and Templates
controls.description: ESAs shall develop common draft regulatory technical standards for the content and time limits of incident reports.

controls.title: Voluntary Notification of Significant Cyber Threats
controls.description: Financial entities may, on a voluntary basis, notify the relevant competent authority of significant cyber threats that they deem to be relevant.

controls.title: General Requirements for Digital Operational Resilience Testing
controls.description: Financial entities shall establish, maintain and review a sound and comprehensive digital operational resilience testing programme as an integral part of the ICT risk management framework.

controls.title: Testing of ICT Tools and Systems
controls.description: The digital operational resilience testing programme shall include a range of assessments, tests, methodologies, practices and tools including vulnerability assessments and scans, open source analyses, network security assessments, gap analyses, physical security reviews, source code reviews, scenario-based tests, compatibility testing, performance testing, end-to-end testing and penetration testing.

controls.title: Advanced Testing of ICT Tools, Systems and Processes based on TLPT
controls.description: Financial entities identified as significant shall carry out threat-led penetration testing (TLPT) at least every 3 years covering critical or important functions.

controls.title: General Principles
controls.description: Financial entities shall manage ICT third-party risk as an integral component of ICT risk within their ICT risk management framework.

controls.title: Preliminary Assessment of ICT Concentration Risk
controls.description: Before entering into a contractual arrangement on the use of ICT services, financial entities shall identify and assess all relevant risks, including whether the contractual arrangement may lead to ICT concentration risk.

controls.title: Key Contractual Provisions
controls.description: The rights and obligations of the financial entity and of the ICT third-party service provider shall be clearly allocated and set out in writing. The contract shall include provisions on accessibility, availability, integrity, security and protection of personal data.

controls.title: Designation of Critical ICT Third-Party Service Providers
controls.description: The ESAs shall designate ICT third-party service providers that are critical for financial entities based on systemic importance criteria.

controls.title: Structure of the Oversight Framework
controls.description: The Joint Committee shall establish the Oversight Forum to support the work of the Lead Overseer in monitoring critical ICT third-party service providers.

controls.title: Tasks of the Lead Overseer
controls.description: The Lead Overseer shall assess whether each critical ICT third-party service provider has in place comprehensive, sound and effective rules, procedures, mechanisms and arrangements to manage the ICT risk which it may pose to financial entities.

controls.title: Information-Sharing Arrangements on Cyber Threat Intelligence
controls.description: Financial entities may exchange amongst themselves cyber threat information and intelligence, including indicators of compromise, tactics, techniques, and procedures.
